Bordeaux vineyards have harvested grapes for wine over centuries.

B1.definition_en: An alcoholic drink consisting of a spirit or spirits mixed with other ingredients, such as fruit juice or cream.

B2.evp_def: A white or rosé sparkling wine produced exclusively in the Champagne region of France.
B2.definition_en: A white or rosé sparkling wine produced exclusively in the Champagne region of France.
examples: They popped a bottle of vintage champagne to toast the anniversary.
Fine streaming bubbles rise gracefully in a chilled flute of champagne.

B2.evp_def: Having the caffeine extracted or naturally absent.

B2.definition_zh: 脱咖啡因的，无咖啡因的

B2.evp_def: The year or place in which wine, especially wine of high quality, was produced.
B2.definition_en: The year or place in which wine, especially wine of high quality, was produced.

C2.evp_def: A drink poured out as an offering to a deity; also humorously used to denote alcoholic beverages.
C2.definition_en: A drink poured out as an offering to a deity; also humorously used to denote alcoholic beverages.
C2.definition_zh: 奠酒，祭酒；（幽默）畅饮的酒水
examples: The ancient Greek priest poured a libation of dark wine upon the altar.
Colleagues gathered at the lounge to enjoy refreshing weekend libations.

A1.definition_en: A hollow muscular organ that pumps the blood through the circulatory system by rhythmic contraction.

A1.definition_en: Each of a pair of globular organs in the head through which humans see.

A2.definition_en: An organ of soft nervous tissue contained in the skull, coordinating sensation and intellectual activity.

A2.definition_en: Any of the pieces of hard, whitish tissue making up the skeleton in humans.

B1.definition_en: Each of the pair of organs situated within the rib cage, allowing oxygen exchange with blood.

B1.evp_def: Each of a pair of organs in the abdominal cavity that excrete urine and regulate electrolyte balance.
B1.definition_en: Each of a pair of organs in the abdominal cavity that excrete urine and regulate electrolyte balance.

C1.evp_def: A layer at the back of the eyeball sensitive to light, triggering nerve impulses via optic nerves.
C1.definition_en: A layer at the back of the eyeball sensitive to light, triggering nerve impulses via optic nerves.

C2.evp_def: The part of the brain at the back of the skull coordinating muscular activity and balance.
C2.definition_en: The part of the brain at the back of the skull coordinating muscular activity and balance.

C2.evp_def: The muscular tube connecting the throat with the stomach.
C2.definition_en: The muscular tube connecting the throat with the stomach.

C2.evp_def: Each of the series of small bones forming the backbone, having several projections for articulation.
C2.definition_en: Each of the series of small bones forming the backbone, having several projections for articulation.

A1.evp_def: A current medium of exchange in the form of coins and banknotes.
A1.definition_en: A current medium of exchange in the form of coins and banknotes.

B2.evp_def: A general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing power of money.

C1.evp_def: The availability of liquid assets to a market or company; the ease with which assets convert to cash.
C1.definition_en: The availability of liquid assets to a market or company; the ease with which assets convert to cash.

C2.evp_def: Persistent high inflation combined with high unemployment and stagnant demand in a country's economy.
C2.definition_en: Persistent high inflation combined with high unemployment and stagnant demand in a country's economy.
C2.definition_zh: 滞胀（经济停滞与通胀并存）

Policymakers face agonizing trade-offs when combating stagflation.

A1.evp_def: Feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.
A1.definition_en: Feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.

A1.evp_def: Feeling or showing sorrow; unhappy.
A1.definition_en: Feeling or showing sorrow; unhappy.

A2.evp_def: Feeling or showing strong annoyance, displeasure, or hostility.
A2.definition_en: Feeling or showing strong annoyance, displeasure, or hostility.

A2.evp_def: Very enthusiastic and eager.

examples: The team was ecstatic and excited about qualifying for the finals.

B1.evp_def: Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.
B1.definition_en: Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.
examples: Try not to be jealous of other people's overnight success.

B1.evp_def: Feeling awkward, self-conscious, or ashamed.
B1.definition_en: Feeling awkward, self-conscious, or ashamed.
examples: He felt deeply embarrassed after mispronouncing the keynote speaker's name.

B2.evp_def: Characterized by or exhibiting a sentimental yearning for the happiness felt in a former place, time, or situation.
B2.definition_en: Characterized by or exhibiting a sentimental yearning for the happiness felt in a former place, time, or situation.
examples: Hearing the vintage jazz tune made him feel deeply nostalgic.
Flipping through grandmother's photo albums evokes nostalgic warmth.

B2.evp_def: The complete loss or absence of hope.
B2.definition_en: The complete loss or absence of hope.
B2.definition_zh: 绝望，令人绝望的人或事

Kind words from a mentor rescued the student from despair.

C1.evp_def: The state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled.
C1.definition_en: The state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled.
examples: Watching mountain peaks shrouded in morning mist brought immense serenity.
Her innate serenity steadied the entire emergency team.

C1.evp_def: Bitter indignation at having been treated unfairly.
C1.definition_en: Bitter indignation at having been treated unfairly.

C1.evp_def: A state of intense excitement and happiness.
C1.definition_en: A state of intense excitement and happiness.

The euphoria of championship victory lasted for weeks.

C2.evp_def: A feeling of pensive sadness, typically with no obvious cause.
C2.definition_en: A feeling of pensive sadness, typically with no obvious cause.
examples: Chopin's nocturnes convey a haunting lyrical melancholy.
An autumn drizzle infused the quiet streets with gentle melancholy.

C2.evp_def: A feeling of intense irritation or annoyance.
C2.definition_en: A feeling of intense irritation or annoyance.

A1.evp_def: a tall plant that has a wooden trunk and branches that grow leaves

A2.evp_def: the weather conditions typical of a particular place

A2.evp_def: to keep someone or something safe from harm, damage, or illness
A2.definition_en: To guard against destruction, peril, or deterioration.

B1.evp_def: damage caused to water, air, etc. by harmful substances or waste

B1.evp_def: to collect and treat rubbish to produce useful materials again
B1.definition_en: To reclaim, process, and convert scrap materials into useful new goods.

Advanced facilities recycle lithium-ion vehicle batteries with high efficiency.

B2.evp_def: the number and types of plants and animals that exist in a particular area
B2.definition_en: The variety, genetic richness, and ecological complexity of living species in an environment.

Preserving biodiversity ensures ecological resilience against viral contagions.

B2.evp_def: causing little or no damage to the environment and able to continue for a long time
B2.definition_en: Capable of being sustained long-term without depleting natural reserves or ecological vitality.

C1.evp_def: all the living things in an area and the way they affect each other and the environment
C1.definition_en: A biological community of interacting organisms and their physical abiotic environment.

C2.evp_def: caused or produced by humans

C2.definition_zh: 人为的，由人类活动引起的

A2.definition_en: To request something to be supplied or served in an eating establishment.

B1.evp_def: one of the foods that you use to make a particular food or dish

B2.evp_def: a style of cooking associated with a particular country or region

B2.evp_def: tasting pleasant enough to eat or drink

B2.definition_zh: 可口的，合心意的，美味的

The committee sought a compromise that would prove palatable to all parties.

C1.evp_def: the art or practice of cooking and eating good food

C1.evp_def: a person who knows a lot about and enjoys one of the arts, food, drink, etc.
C1.definition_en: An expert judge in matters of culinary taste, vintage wines, or fine aesthetics.

Coffee connoisseurs value single-origin beans roasted to perfection.

C2.evp_def: devoted to the pursuit of sensual pleasure, especially to good food and comfort

C2.definition_zh: 享乐主义的，讲究饮食的，美食家的

C2.evp_def: connected with the sense of taste

examples: Tasting menus engage both olfactory and gustatory faculties in harmony.
The dessert was a sensory spectacle, creating a memorable gustatory impression.

A1.evp_def: A long curved fruit which grows in clusters and has soft pulpy flesh and yellow skin when ripe.

A2.evp_def: substance used to cure disease or relieve pain

A2.evp_def: to become healthy after an illness or injury

B1.evp_def: a change in body or mind indicating a disease

B2.evp_def: persisting for a long time or constantly recurring

B2.evp_def: to restore to health or normal life through therapy
B2.definition_en: To restore an injured or impaired individual to health or functional capacity through targeted therapy.

C1.evp_def: a widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community
C1.definition_en: A widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a population within a given period.

Glaze tender pork tenderloin with apple cider and mustard.

B1.definition_en: A large edible fish with pink flesh, celebrated for rich omega-3 fatty acids.
examples: Pan-sear wild Atlantic salmon skin-side down until wonderfully crispy.
Smoked salmon and cream cheese are beloved bagel toppings.

B1.evp_def: A small free-swimming crustacean with an elongated body, highly prized as seafood.
B1.definition_en: A small free-swimming crustacean with an elongated body, highly prized as seafood.
examples: Garlic butter shrimp sautéed with parsley cooks in under four minutes.
The coastal town hosts an annual festival celebrating freshly caught shrimp.

B1.evp_def: The meat of a young sheep eaten as food.
B1.definition_en: The meat of a young sheep eaten as food.

Marinate lamb skewers with cumin and coriander before charcoal grilling.

B1.evp_def: A large predatory oceanic fish of the mackerel family, heavily fished commercially.
B1.definition_en: A large predatory oceanic fish of the mackerel family, heavily fished commercially.

B2.definition_en: A large marine crustacean with a cylindrical body and stalked eyes, possessing two large pincers.

Dip steamed lobster claws in warm clarified drawn butter.

B2.evp_def: Any of a number of bivalve mollusks with rough irregular shells, eaten raw as food.
B2.definition_en: Any of a number of bivalve mollusks with rough irregular shells, eaten raw as food.
examples: Freshly shucked coastal oysters served over shaved ice with mignonette.

C1.evp_def: The edible meat of a deer.
C1.definition_en: The edible meat of a deer.
examples: Roasted loin of venison pairs magnificently with blackberry reduction sauce.
Venison is exceptionally lean compared to conventional feedlot beef.

C1.evp_def: A small, shoaling fish of commercial importance, often salted, cured, and canned in oil.
C1.definition_en: A small, shoaling fish of commercial importance, often salted, cured, and canned in oil.
examples: Melted salted anchovies lend profound umami richness to Caesar dressing.
Neapolitan pizza toppings frequently incorporate cured anchovy fillets.

C2.evp_def: Cold cooked, cured, or smoked meats considered collectively, including pâtés, terrines, and salamis.
C2.definition_en: Cold cooked, cured, or smoked meats considered collectively, including pâtés, terrines, and salamis.

examples: The sommelier assembled an artisanal charcuterie board featuring prosciutto and duck rillettes.
French charcuterie traditions preserve ancestral curing craftsmanship.

A1.evp_def: A liquid dish, typically made by boiling meat, fish, or vegetables in stock or water.
A1.definition_en: A liquid dish, typically made by boiling meat, fish, or vegetables in stock or water.
examples: A bowl of hot chicken noodle soup soothes a winter cold.
Creamy mushroom soup was served with warm crusty baguettes.

A1.evp_def: A cold dish of various raw or cooked vegetables seasoned with oil, vinegar, or other dressing.
A1.definition_en: A cold dish of various raw or cooked vegetables seasoned with oil, vinegar, or other dressing.
examples: Toss crisp romaine lettuce with vinaigrette for a refreshing green salad.
A Greek salad features ripe tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and feta cheese.

A1.evp_def: Food made of flour, water, and yeast or another leavening agent, baked.
A1.definition_en: Food made of flour, water, and yeast or another leavening agent, baked.
examples: Warm sourdough bread with salted butter is irresistible.

A2.evp_def: The sweet course eaten at the end of a meal.
A2.definition_en: The sweet course eaten at the end of a meal.

Tiramisu is Italy's most celebrated coffee-flavored dessert.

A2.evp_def: A dish originally from Italy consisting of dough made from durum wheat and water, cooked in boiling water.
A2.definition_en: A dish originally from Italy consisting of dough made from durum wheat and water, cooked in boiling water.
examples: Cook the artisan pasta al dente before tossing with basil pesto.

B1.evp_def: A small dish of food served before a main meal to stimulate one's appetite.
B1.definition_en: A small dish of food served before a main meal to stimulate one's appetite.

We ordered a medley of hot appetizers to share among our group.

B2.evp_def: The main course of a meal in North America, or a dish served before the main course in France.
B2.definition_en: The main course of a meal in North America, or a dish served before the main course in France.
examples: For the entree, patrons may select between Chilean sea bass or aged ribeye.
Every plated entree was executed with Michelin-star precision.

B2.evp_def: To soak food in a marinade consisting of acid, oil, and spices before cooking.
B2.definition_en: To soak food in a marinade consisting of acid, oil, and spices before cooking.
examples: Marinate the flank steak overnight to tenderize fibrous muscle tissue.
Tofu absorbs savory aromatics effortlessly when left to marinate.

B2.evp_def: Of a kind or standard suitable for a gourmet; of high quality and refined flavor.
B2.definition_en: Of a kind or standard suitable for a gourmet; of high quality and refined flavor.
examples: The boutique market stocks gourmet imported olive oils.

C1.evp_def: Something considered choice to eat, typically being rare, expensive, or culturally prized.
C1.definition_en: Something considered choice to eat, typically being rare, expensive, or culturally prized.
examples: Black truffles shaved over fresh egg tagliatelle are a prized winter delicacy.
Local markets offer rare regional delicacies difficult to source elsewhere.

C2.evp_def: A wine steward or trained specialist in fine wine service and pairing.
C2.definition_en: A wine steward or trained specialist in fine wine service and pairing.
examples: The head sommelier recommended a dry Riesling to complement the poached turbot.
Becoming a master sommelier requires passing legendary blind tasting exams.

A2.evp_def: The quality or state of being in accordance with fact or reality.
A2.definition_en: The quality or state of being in accordance with fact or reality.
examples: Philosophers have debated the nature of objective truth for millennia.
Science seeks empirical truth through rigorous observation.

A2.evp_def: The power of the mind to think, understand, and form judgments by a process of logic.
A2.definition_en: The power of the mind to think, understand, and form judgments by a process of logic.
examples: Enlightenment philosophers elevated human reason above superstition.

B1.evp_def: Reasoning conducted or assessed according to strict principles of validity.
B1.definition_en: Reasoning conducted or assessed according to strict principles of validity.
examples: Aristotelian logic laid the groundwork for modern formal syllogisms.
There was an inescapable flaw in the opponent's core logic.

B2.evp_def: Moral principles that govern a person's behavior or the conducting of an activity.
B2.definition_en: Moral principles that govern a person's behavior or the conducting of an activity.
examples: Bioethics examines ethical dilemmas surrounding genetic engineering.
A philosopher must weigh conflicting duties in virtue ethics.

B2.evp_def: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.
B2.definition_en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.
examples: Descartes championed rational thought as the prime foundation of knowledge.
Emotions should be balanced by rational inquiry.

B2.evp_def: Principles concerning the distinction between right and wrong or good and bad behavior.
B2.definition_en: Principles concerning the distinction between right and wrong or good and bad behavior.
examples: The book explores whether universal morality exists without divine decree.

C1.evp_def: Relating to human existence or the existentialist philosophy asserting individual freedom and purpose.
C1.definition_en: Relating to human existence or the existentialist philosophy asserting individual freedom and purpose.
C1.definition_zh: 存在主义的，关于人类存在的
examples: Sartre addressed the existential burden of absolute personal freedom.
Climate change poses an acute existential crisis for planetary biodiversity.

C1.evp_def: The branch of philosophy concerned with knowledge, belief, and the justification of truth claims.
C1.definition_en: The branch of philosophy concerned with knowledge, belief, and the justification of truth claims.
examples: Epistemology asks how we can reliably distinguish knowledge from mere opinion.
Kant revolutionized epistemology by proposing synthetic a priori judgments.

C1.evp_def: The rejection of all religious and moral principles, often in the belief that life is meaningless.
C1.definition_en: The rejection of all religious and moral principles, often in the belief that life is meaningless.
examples: Nietzsche examined the historical emergence of European nihilism.
Existentialism attempted to overcome nihilism by creating subjective purpose.

C1.evp_def: Designed to be useful or practical rather than attractive; relating to the doctrine that actions are right if they benefit the majority.
C1.definition_en: Designed to be useful or practical rather than attractive; relating to the doctrine that actions are right if they benefit the majority.
examples: Utilitarian ethics judges an action by its net contribution to collective happiness.

C2.evp_def: The discourse between two opposing viewpoints seeking to establish truth through reasoned arguments.
C2.definition_en: The discourse between two opposing viewpoints seeking to establish truth through reasoned arguments.
examples: Hegelian dialectic synthesizes thesis and antithesis into higher comprehension.
Socrates employed rigorous dialectic to expose hidden contradictions.

C2.evp_def: The philosophical idea that only one's own mind is sure to exist.
C2.definition_en: The philosophical idea that only one's own mind is sure to exist.
examples: Epistemological skepticism taken to its absolute extreme arrives at solipsism.
He dismissed solipsism as an unlivable intellectual novelty.

C2.evp_def: The branch of metaphysics dealing with the nature of being and reality.
C2.definition_en: The branch of metaphysics dealing with the nature of being and reality.
examples: Ontology investigates what categories of entities fundamentally exist.

A1.evp_def: To give a formal expression of opinion or choice in an election.
A1.definition_en: To give a formal expression of opinion or choice in an election.
examples: Every eligible citizen has a democratic right to vote.
Millions turned out to vote in yesterday's national ballot.

A1.evp_def: The person who leads or commands a group, organization, or country.
A1.definition_en: The person who leads or commands a group, organization, or country.
examples: World leaders convened to sign the historic peace accord.

A2.evp_def: The governing body of a nation, state, or community.
A2.definition_en: The governing body of a nation, state, or community.
examples: The new government promised to prioritize healthcare reform.
Local government administers community libraries and road maintenance.

A2.evp_def: A legally recognized subject or national of a state or commonwealth.
A2.definition_en: A legally recognized subject or national of a state or commonwealth.
examples: Active citizens participate routinely in civic forums.

B1.evp_def: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government, party, or business.
B1.definition_en: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government, party, or business.
examples: The foreign policy focuses on strengthening bilateral trade ties.
Strict environmental policies have curtailed industrial pollution.

B1.evp_def: An organized course of political actions toward winning election or achieving a policy goal.
B1.definition_en: An organized course of political actions toward winning election or achieving a policy goal.
examples: The mayoral campaign organized rallies across every district.
Digital grassroots fundraising transformed modern election campaigns.

B2.evp_def: A system of government by the whole population typically through elected representatives.
B2.definition_en: A system of government by the whole population typically through elected representatives.
examples: A free press serves as an indispensable pillar of healthy democracy.
The transition toward constitutional democracy took several turbulent decades.

B2.evp_def: A general vote by the electorate on a single political question referred for a direct decision.
B2.definition_en: A general vote by the electorate on a single political question referred for a direct decision.
examples: The citizens voted in favor of constitutional reform during the referendum.
Holding a nationwide referendum settled the longstanding territorial controversy.

B2.evp_def: The profession, activity, or skill of managing international relations.
B2.definition_en: The profession, activity, or skill of managing international relations.
examples: Diplomacy prevailed where military posturing had failed.
Ambassadors must balance firmness with subtle cultural diplomacy.

B2.evp_def: A system of government in which most decisions are made by state officials rather than elected representatives.
B2.definition_en: A system of government in which most decisions are made by state officials rather than elected representatives.
examples: Excessive bureaucratic paperwork stifled small business creation.

C1.evp_def: Favoring or enforcing strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom.
C1.definition_en: Favoring or enforcing strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom.
examples: The report documented the erosion of civil liberties under the authoritarian regime.
Dissidents faced severe censorship in authoritarian states.

C1.evp_def: The supreme power or authority of a state to govern itself or another state.
C1.definition_en: The supreme power or authority of a state to govern itself or another state.
examples: Treaties must respect the territorial sovereignty of independent member states.
Economic interdependence sometimes complicates traditional concepts of state sovereignty.

C2.evp_def: To manipulate the boundaries of an electoral constituency so as to favor one party or class.
C2.definition_en: To manipulate the boundaries of an electoral constituency so as to favor one party or class.
C2.definition_zh: 不公地改划选区以谋私利
examples: Partisan legislatures attempted to gerrymander congressional districts before the election.
Courts struck down the gerrymandered electoral map for violating voter equity.

C2.evp_def: A small group of people having control of a country, organization, or institution.
C2.definition_en: A small group of people having control of a country, organization, or institution.
C2.definition_zh: 寡头政治，寡头垄断集团
examples: Critics warned that astronomical campaign donations risk turning democracy into an oligarchy.
The transition from monarchy led directly into a commercial oligarchy.

A1.evp_def: The element of a person that enables them to be aware of the world and their experiences, to think, and to feel.
A1.definition_en: The element of a person that enables them to be aware of the world and their experiences, to think, and to feel.
examples: Keep an open mind when evaluating novel concepts.
A healthy body supports a sound mind.

A2.evp_def: A series of thoughts, images, and sensations occurring in a person's mind during sleep.
A2.definition_en: A series of thoughts, images, and sensations occurring in a person's mind during sleep.
examples: I had a vivid dream about exploring ancient library corridors.
Dream analysis was central to early psychoanalysis.

A2.evp_def: The way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially toward others.
A2.definition_en: The way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially toward others.
examples: Behavioral psychologists study the relationship between environment and action.

B1.evp_def: The faculty by which the mind stores and remembers information.
B1.definition_en: The faculty by which the mind stores and remembers information.
examples: Working memory allows humans to retain cognitive clues temporarily.
She has an extraordinary memory for historical dates.

B1.evp_def: A feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease typically about an imminent event or uncertain outcome.
B1.definition_en: A feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease typically about an imminent event or uncertain outcome.
examples: Mindfulness meditation can substantially reduce generalized anxiety.
Exam anxiety often prevents students from performing at their best.

B2.evp_def: Concerning the part of the mind of which one is not fully aware but which influences actions and feelings.
B2.definition_en: Concerning the part of the mind of which one is not fully aware but which influences actions and feelings.
examples: Subconscious biases can subtly influence hiring deliberations.
Advertising frequently appeals to subconscious desires.

B2.evp_def: Relating to conscious mental processes of cognition, perception, memory, and judgment.
B2.definition_en: Relating to conscious mental processes of cognition, perception, memory, and judgment.
examples: Cognitive behavioral therapy helps reframe negative mental patterns.
Sleep deprivation damages cognitive processing speed.

B2.evp_def: A deeply distressing or disturbing emotional or mental experience.
B2.definition_en: A deeply distressing or disturbing emotional or mental experience.
examples: Psychologists specialize in helping refugees heal from wartime trauma.
Early childhood trauma can cast long shadows over adult life.

B2.evp_def: Tending to be predominantly concerned with one's own mental life rather than external surroundings.
B2.definition_en: Tending to be predominantly concerned with one's own mental life rather than external surroundings.
examples: Introverted students often prefer deep solitary research to large group discussions.
Being introverted is a temperament, not a social deficit.

B2.evp_def: A thing or event that evokes a specific functional reaction in an organ or tissue.
B2.definition_en: A thing or event that evokes a specific functional reaction in an organ or tissue.
examples: Pavlov discovered conditioned responses to auditory stimuli.

C1.evp_def: The examination or observation of one's own mental and emotional processes.
C1.definition_en: The examination or observation of one's own mental and emotional processes.
examples: A quiet evening walk provides space for calm introspection.
Introspection without action can sometimes lead to excessive rumination.

C1.evp_def: The process of releasing, and thereby providing relief from, strong or repressed emotions.
C1.definition_en: The process of releasing, and thereby providing relief from, strong or repressed emotions.
C1.definition_zh: 精神宣泄，净化，宣泄作用
examples: Weeping during the tragic theatrical finale provided an emotional catharsis.
Artistic creation often functions as an avenue for psychological catharsis.

C1.evp_def: Below the threshold of conscious perception, though still having an influence on the mind.
C1.definition_en: Below the threshold of conscious perception, though still having an influence on the mind.
C1.definition_zh: 下意识的，潜意识感知的，阈下的
examples: The documentary examined how background melodies exert subliminal influence.
Subliminal messages are prohibited in mainstream television advertising.

C1.evp_def: A mild mental illness involving symptoms of stress (depression, anxiety, obsessive behavior).
C1.definition_en: A mild mental illness involving symptoms of stress (depression, anxiety, obsessive behavior).
examples: Chronic perfectionism can sometimes border on obsessive neurosis.

C2.evp_def: A severe mental condition characterized by a loss of contact with external reality.
C2.definition_en: A severe mental condition characterized by a loss of contact with external reality.
examples: Acute drug intoxication can occasionally precipitate transient psychosis.
Clinical intervention is paramount during the inaugural onset of psychosis.

A1.evp_def: an electronic machine that can store and work with large amounts of information
A1.definition_en: A programmable electronic device capable of processing information according to stored algorithms.
examples: Modern computers can execute trillions of instructions per second.
She turned on her computer to check today's correspondence.

A1.evp_def: to press a button on a computer mouse
A1.definition_en: To press and release a mouse button or tap an interactive digital screen element.
examples: Click the download button to begin retrieving the installation package.
Double-click the desktop icon to open the workspace.

A2.evp_def: the flat surface on a computer or television where pictures or words are shown
A2.definition_en: The physical visual display interface of an electronic terminal, monitor, or phone.
examples: The OLED screen provides vibrant contrast and rich color accuracy.
Looking at high-brightness screens in the dark causes severe eyestrain.

A2.evp_def: to copy computer files to your computer from the internet
A2.definition_en: To transfer digital data or software from a remote server to a local terminal.
examples: It only took three seconds to download the entire textbook over high-speed fiber.
Always verify digital signatures before executing downloaded binaries.

B1.evp_def: an object or machine that has been invented for a particular purpose
B1.definition_en: A machine, instrument, or piece of hardware engineered for a distinct technical role.
examples: Smart home devices communicate effortlessly over low-latency wireless protocols.
Ensure the peripheral device is securely plugged into an active USB port.

B1.evp_def: to put computer software onto a computer
B1.definition_en: To set up software or physical equipment ready for execution or operational use.
examples: Please install the latest security patch before connecting to the enterprise intranet.
The setup wizard will install all essential libraries automatically.

B2.evp_def: a set of mathematical instructions used by computers to solve problems
B2.definition_en: A well-defined finite procedure or sequence of logic rules formulated to solve a computational challenge.
examples: Search engines rely on complex ranking algorithms to index web pages.
The recommendation algorithm personalizes audio playlists according to listening habits.

B2.evp_def: to make two or more things happen at the same time or speed
B2.definition_en: To coordinate clocks, concurrent processes, or distributed datasets to maintain parity.
examples: Cloud drives automatically synchronize modified files across all registered devices.
Distributed nodes must synchronize their logical clocks to preserve transactional consistency.

C1.evp_def: independent and having the power to make your own decisions; self-operating
C1.definition_en: Operating without direct continuous human control; self-governing and independent.
C1.definition_zh: 自主的，自动驾驶的，自治的
examples: Autonomous delivery drones navigate metropolitan corridors using computer vision and lidar.
The agent was granted autonomous permissions to optimize database queries.

C1.evp_def: to change electronic information into a secret code
C1.definition_en: To convert plain data into cryptographic ciphertext to prevent unauthorized access.
examples: The banking protocol encrypts customer credentials with 256-bit AES encryption.
Always encrypt sensitive storage partitions prior to cloud synchronization.

C2.evp_def: enabling someone to discover or learn something for themselves through practical methods
C2.definition_en: Serving to discover or stimulate investigation; problem-solving via rule-of-thumb rather than rigid proofs.
examples: Antivirus software deploys heuristic scanning to detect zero-day malware patterns.
Heuristics provide approximate solutions when optimal calculations are computationally intractable.

C2.evp_def: present, appearing, or found everywhere
C2.definition_en: Existing or being encountered everywhere simultaneously; omnipresent.
C2.definition_zh: 无所不在的，普遍存在的
examples: Smartphones have evolved from luxury items into ubiquitous everyday utilities.
Microchips have become ubiquitous across automotive and home appliance industries.

A1.evp_def: a piece of paper that gives you the right to travel on a train, bus, etc.
A1.definition_en: A pass entitling the holder to admission to a venue or transit on passenger transport.
examples: I booked a train ticket to Edinburgh this morning.
Do you have your boarding ticket ready for the gate agent?

A1.evp_def: to reach a place, especially at the end of a journey
A1.definition_en: To reach a destination; to come to the end of a journey.
examples: The international flight arrived precisely on schedule.
Call me the moment you arrive at the airport.

A2.evp_def: the bags and suitcases that a traveler carries
A2.definition_en: Suitcases, bags, or other items used to carry a traveler's belongings.
examples: Passengers are advised never to leave their luggage unattended.
We retrieved our luggage at carousel number four.

A2.evp_def: to make something happen later than planned
A2.definition_en: To postpone until a later date or time; to cause to be tardy.
examples: Severe thunderstorms delayed the flight by nearly two hours.
Don't delay making your reservations before prices surge.

B1.evp_def: the place where someone or something is going
B1.definition_en: The ultimate endpoint to which someone or something travels.
examples: Kyoto remains one of the world's most sought-after travel destinations.
After ten hours on the road, they finally reached their destination.

B1.evp_def: to make the same trip regularly between work and home
B1.definition_en: To travel regularly over some distance between one's home and place of work.
examples: She commutes daily by express subway from New Jersey into Manhattan.
Remote work allows engineers to skip the stressful morning commute.

B2.evp_def: a detailed plan or route of a journey
B2.definition_en: A detailed schedule, route, or proposed outline of a journey.
examples: The tour guide distributed a comprehensive itinerary for the weekend excursion.
We had to modify our itinerary when mountain passes were blocked by snow.

B2.evp_def: so crowded with traffic or people as to hinder freedom of movement
B2.definition_en: Overcrowded, clogged, or impeded by heavy traffic or volume.
examples: Downtown streets become notoriously congested during rush hour.
The city implemented toll lanes to relieve congested thoroughfares.

C1.evp_def: a temporary stay
C1.definition_en: A temporary residence or brief visit in a foreign or unfamiliar locality.
examples: During his brief sojourn in Florence, he wrote two historical novels.
Her summer sojourn in Provence inspired an entire culinary collection.

C1.evp_def: to cause something to happen faster
C1.definition_en: To accelerate the process or dispatch of; to hasten progress.
examples: Border control introduced biometric e-gates to expedite customs clearance.
You can pay an express fee to expedite passport renewal.

C2.evp_def: traveling from place to place, especially working in different places
C2.definition_en: Wandering, traveling from place to place, especially in connection with work.
C2.definition_zh: 巡游的，流动的，走街串巷的
examples: As an international photojournalist, she lived a thoroughly peripatetic life.
His peripatetic career required constant relocation across four continents.

C2.evp_def: a long and meandering journey
C2.definition_en: A journey, travel, or wandering around from one place to another.
examples: His solitary peregrinations across the Tibetan plateau are chronicled in his diary.
After years of restless peregrination, the explorer finally settled down.

A1.evp_def: A starchy plant tuber that is one of the most important food crops worldwide.
A1.definition_en: A starchy plant tuber that is one of the most important food crops worldwide.
examples: Mashed potatoes seasoned with butter and chives accompany the steak.
Boil the potatoes until tender to make potato salad.

A1.evp_def: A glossy red, or occasionally yellow, pulpy edible fruit eaten as a vegetable or in salad.
A1.definition_en: A glossy red, or occasionally yellow, pulpy edible fruit eaten as a vegetable or in salad.

A2.evp_def: A tapering orange-colored root eaten as a vegetable.
A2.definition_en: A tapering orange-colored root eaten as a vegetable.

A2.evp_def: A swollen edible bulb with a pungent taste and smell, composed of several concentric layers.
A2.definition_en: A swollen edible bulb with a pungent taste and smell, composed of several concentric layers.

A2.evp_def: A cultivated plant with a round head of dense green or reddish leaves.
A2.definition_en: A cultivated plant with a round head of dense green or reddish leaves.
examples: Shredded red cabbage adds vibrant crunch to winter salads.

A2.evp_def: A long, green-skinned fruit with watery flesh, usually eaten raw in salads.
A2.definition_en: A long, green-skinned fruit with watery flesh, usually eaten raw in salads.

B1.evp_def: A cultivated variety of cabbage bearing heads of green or purplish flower buds.
B1.definition_en: A cultivated variety of cabbage bearing heads of green or purplish flower buds.
examples: Steamed broccoli preserves vital micronutrients and retains a vibrant green hue.

B1.evp_def: An edible flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae with dark green succulent leaves.
B1.definition_en: An edible flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae with dark green succulent leaves.
examples: Fresh baby spinach wilts within seconds when tossed into hot soup.
Spinach is renowned for iron and folate content.

B1.evp_def: The purple egg-shaped fruit of a tropical Old World plant, eaten as a vegetable.
B1.definition_en: The purple egg-shaped fruit of a tropical Old World plant, eaten as a vegetable.
examples: Roasted eggplant pureed with tahini produces rich baba ghanoush.

B2.evp_def: A tall plant of the lily family with fine feathery foliage, cultivated for its tender edible young shoots.
B2.definition_en: A tall plant of the lily family with fine feathery foliage, cultivated for its tender edible young shoots.
examples: Grill tender green asparagus spears with a drizzle of lemon oil.
Snap off the woody bottom ends of asparagus before cooking.

B2.evp_def: A small variety of vegetable marrow; a summer squash with green skin.
B2.definition_en: A small variety of vegetable marrow; a summer squash with green skin.
examples: Spiralized zucchini ribbons make a nutritious low-carb pasta alternative.
Bake grated zucchini into moist cinnamon loaves.

C1.evp_def: A European plant cultivated for its large thistle-like flower heads, the fleshy bases of which are edible.
C1.definition_en: A European plant cultivated for its large thistle-like flower heads, the fleshy bases of which are edible.
examples: Steam whole globe artichokes and dip the fleshy bract leaves in garlic butter.
Marinated artichoke hearts are standard fixtures in Mediterranean antipasti.

C2.evp_def: A cultivated cabbage of a variety with an edible swollen stem resembling a turnip.

Communities planted ten thousand native trees to curb soil erosion.

items.evp_def: to fall as drops of water from clouds
items.definition_en: To precipitate water droplets from clouds.
examples: It started to rain gently as the autumn twilight descended.
If it rains tomorrow, we will relocate the ceremony indoors.

items.evp_def: the weather conditions typical of a particular place
items.definition_en: The meteorological trends, average temperature, and rainfall of a locale over decades.
examples: Mediterranean climates feature temperate wet winters and arid summers.
Accelerating climate shifts threaten fragile alpine biomes.

items.evp_def: to keep someone or something safe from harm, damage, or illness
items.definition_en: To guard against destruction, peril, or deterioration.
examples: Marine reserves are established to protect coral reefs from predatory trawling.
Wear high-factor sunscreen to protect your skin from ultraviolet rays.

items.evp_def: damage caused to water, air, etc. by harmful substances or waste
items.definition_en: The contamination of air, water, or earth by detrimental synthetic toxins.
examples: Stricter vehicle emissions standards reduced particulate air pollution significantly.
Plastic pollution wreaks catastrophic havoc on pelagic marine ecosystems.

items.evp_def: to collect and treat rubbish to produce useful materials again
items.definition_en: To reclaim, process, and convert scrap materials into useful new goods.
examples: The community incentivizes residents to recycle glass, paper, and aluminum.
Advanced facilities recycle lithium-ion vehicle batteries with high efficiency.

items.evp_def: the number and types of plants and animals that exist in a particular area
items.definition_en: The variety, genetic richness, and ecological complexity of living species in an environment.
examples: Amazonian rainforests harbor the densest terrestrial biodiversity on our planet.
Preserving biodiversity ensures ecological resilience against viral contagions.

items.evp_def: causing little or no damage to the environment and able to continue for a long time
items.definition_en: Capable of being sustained long-term without depleting natural reserves or ecological vitality.
examples: Hydropower and geothermal energy provide dependable sustainable power grids.
Sustainable forestry practices mandate planting two saplings for each felled tree.

items.evp_def: all the living things in an area and the way they affect each other and the environment
items.definition_en: A biological community of interacting organisms and their physical abiotic environment.
examples: Mangrove wetlands act as a vital buffer and dynamic nursery ecosystem.
Introducing invasive predator species disrupts the delicate equilibrium of island ecosystems.

items.evp_def: to reduce something in size or amount, especially supplies of energy, money, etc.
items.definition_en: To drastically diminish the stock, supply, or natural capacity of.
examples: Over-extraction of groundwater threatens to deplete regional subterranean aquifers.
Aggressive commercial fishing quotas were enacted before stocks were completely depleted.

items.evp_def: caused or produced by humans
items.definition_en: Originating in human activity; caused or generated by anthropogenic emissions.
items.definition_zh: 人为的，由人类活动引起的
examples: Scientists documented unmistakable spikes in anthropogenic greenhouse gas concentrations.
Accelerated coastal subsidence is exacerbated by anthropogenic industrial drainage.

items.evp_def: the hardening of tissue or ocean corals due to deposits of calcium salts
items.definition_en: The deposition of insoluble lime salts; process by which marine shells and skeletal structures mineralize.
examples: Ocean acidification impairs the biological calcification rates of shell-forming mollusks.
Coral reef calcification has slowed markedly as ocean surface temperatures increase.

items.evp_def: a continuous pain in your head
items.definition_en: A continuous dull or throbbing ache located within the cranial region.
examples: Working twelve hours in front of glare gave her a throbbing headache.
He took an aspirin and rested in a dim room to soothe his headache.

items.evp_def: to cause pain or injury
items.definition_en: To experience or cause localized physical pain or distress.
items.definition_zh: 感到疼痛，受伤害，使受伤
examples: My knee hurts whenever I ascend steep flights of stairs.
Be careful with that scalpel; you might hurt yourself.

items.evp_def: substance used to cure disease or relieve pain
items.definition_en: Any pharmacological compound, drug, or clinical treatment formulated to alleviate disease.
examples: Take two tablets of this prescribed medicine after meals.
Breakthroughs in genomic medicine have transformed targeted cancer therapy.

items.evp_def: to become healthy after an illness or injury
items.definition_en: To regain normal health, vitality, or physical composure following disease or injury.
examples: The patient recovered completely within two weeks post-surgery.
Adequate sleep and balanced nutrition allow muscles to recover rapidly.

items.evp_def: a change in body or mind indicating a disease
items.definition_en: A subjective physical sensation indicating disease or physiological aberration.
examples: Persistent dry cough and high fever are common symptoms of respiratory infection.
Prompt diagnosis occurs when clinicians recognize atypical early symptoms.

items.evp_def: to specify medicine or treatment in writing
items.definition_en: To formally authorize medical treatment or the dispensing of pharmaceutical substances.
examples: The physician prescribed an antihistamine to treat seasonal allergic rhinitis.
Doctors rarely prescribe antibiotics for uncomplicated viral colds.

items.evp_def: persisting for a long time or constantly recurring
items.definition_en: Continuing or persisting over an extended clinical timeline; lingering.
examples: Lifestyle interventions can mitigate the complications of chronic hypertension.
Physical therapy offers meaningful relief to individuals with chronic lumbar pain.

items.evp_def: to restore to health or normal life through therapy
items.definition_en: To restore an injured or impaired individual to health or functional capacity through targeted therapy.
examples: The sports clinic specializes in rehabilitating athletes recovering from ligament tears.
Structured occupational therapy helps stroke survivors rehabilitate motor coordination.

items.evp_def: a widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community
items.definition_en: A widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a population within a given period.
examples: Public health officials deployed contact-tracing to contain the measles epidemic.
Sedentary lifestyle habits have fueled a silent epidemic of type-2 diabetes.

items.evp_def: to make someone very weak and infirm
items.definition_en: To severely weaken, incapacitate, or sap the bodily strength of.
examples: Severe autoimmune flare-ups can debilitate patients if left unmanaged.
Tropical heat debilitated the expedition crew during the march.

items.evp_def: the investigation of the cause or origin of disease
items.definition_en: The cause, set of causes, or scientific causation theory of a medical disorder.
examples: Researchers mapped the molecular etiology of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
Determining the exact bacterial etiology is essential for administering targeted antibiotics.

items.evp_def: a solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases
items.definition_en: A hypothetical remedy, cure-all, or solution for all diseases or problems.
items.definition_zh: 万能药，灵丹妙药，万全之策
examples: There is no single pharmacological panacea for complex metabolic syndromes.
Technology alone is not a panacea for profound socio-economic divides.

items.evp_def: The element of a person that enables them to be aware of the world and their experiences, to think, and to feel.
items.definition_en: The element of a person that enables them to be aware of the world and their experiences, to think, and to feel.
examples: Keep an open mind when evaluating novel concepts.
A healthy body supports a sound mind.

items.evp_def: A series of thoughts, images, and sensations occurring in a person's mind during sleep.
items.definition_en: A series of thoughts, images, and sensations occurring in a person's mind during sleep.
examples: I had a vivid dream about exploring ancient library corridors.
Dream analysis was central to early psychoanalysis.

items.evp_def: The faculty by which the mind stores and remembers information.
items.definition_en: The faculty by which the mind stores and remembers information.
examples: Working memory allows humans to retain cognitive clues temporarily.
She has an extraordinary memory for historical dates.

items.evp_def: A feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease typically about an imminent event or uncertain outcome.
items.definition_en: A feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease typically about an imminent event or uncertain outcome.
examples: Mindfulness meditation can substantially reduce generalized anxiety.
Exam anxiety often prevents students from performing at their best.

items.evp_def: Concerning the part of the mind of which one is not fully aware but which influences actions and feelings.
items.definition_en: Concerning the part of the mind of which one is not fully aware but which influences actions and feelings.
examples: Subconscious biases can subtly influence hiring deliberations.
Advertising frequently appeals to subconscious desires.

items.evp_def: Relating to conscious mental processes of cognition, perception, memory, and judgment.
items.definition_en: Relating to conscious mental processes of cognition, perception, memory, and judgment.
examples: Cognitive behavioral therapy helps reframe negative mental patterns.
Sleep deprivation damages cognitive processing speed.

items.evp_def: A deeply distressing or disturbing emotional or mental experience.
items.definition_en: A deeply distressing or disturbing emotional or mental experience.
examples: Psychologists specialize in helping refugees heal from wartime trauma.
Early childhood trauma can cast long shadows over adult life.

items.evp_def: Tending to be predominantly concerned with one's own mental life rather than external surroundings.
items.definition_en: Tending to be predominantly concerned with one's own mental life rather than external surroundings.
examples: Introverted students often prefer deep solitary research to large group discussions.
Being introverted is a temperament, not a social deficit.

items.evp_def: The examination or observation of one's own mental and emotional processes.
items.definition_en: The examination or observation of one's own mental and emotional processes.
examples: A quiet evening walk provides space for calm introspection.
Introspection without action can sometimes lead to excessive rumination.

items.evp_def: The process of releasing, and thereby providing relief from, strong or repressed emotions.
items.definition_en: The process of releasing, and thereby providing relief from, strong or repressed emotions.
items.definition_zh: 精神宣泄，净化，宣泄作用
examples: Weeping during the tragic theatrical finale provided an emotional catharsis.
Artistic creation often functions as an avenue for psychological catharsis.

items.evp_def: Below the threshold of conscious perception, though still having an influence on the mind.
items.definition_en: Below the threshold of conscious perception, though still having an influence on the mind.
items.definition_zh: 下意识的，潜意识感知的，阈下的
examples: The documentary examined how background melodies exert subliminal influence.
Subliminal messages are prohibited in mainstream television advertising.

items.evp_def: A severe mental condition characterized by a loss of contact with external reality.
items.definition_en: A severe mental condition characterized by a loss of contact with external reality.
examples: Acute drug intoxication can occasionally precipitate transient psychosis.
Clinical intervention is paramount during the inaugural onset of psychosis.

items.evp_def: To give a formal expression of opinion or choice in an election.
items.definition_en: To give a formal expression of opinion or choice in an election.
examples: Every eligible citizen has a democratic right to vote.
Millions turned out to vote in yesterday's national ballot.

items.evp_def: The governing body of a nation, state, or community.
items.definition_en: The governing body of a nation, state, or community.
examples: The new government promised to prioritize healthcare reform.
Local government administers community libraries and road maintenance.

items.evp_def: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government, party, or business.
items.definition_en: A course or principle of action adopted or proposed by a government, party, or business.
examples: The foreign policy focuses on strengthening bilateral trade ties.
Strict environmental policies have curtailed industrial pollution.

items.evp_def: An organized course of political actions toward winning election or achieving a policy goal.
items.definition_en: An organized course of political actions toward winning election or achieving a policy goal.
examples: The mayoral campaign organized rallies across every district.
Digital grassroots fundraising transformed modern election campaigns.

items.evp_def: A system of government by the whole population typically through elected representatives.
items.definition_en: A system of government by the whole population typically through elected representatives.
examples: A free press serves as an indispensable pillar of healthy democracy.
The transition toward constitutional democracy took several turbulent decades.

items.evp_def: A general vote by the electorate on a single political question referred for a direct decision.
items.definition_en: A general vote by the electorate on a single political question referred for a direct decision.
examples: The citizens voted in favor of constitutional reform during the referendum.
Holding a nationwide referendum settled the longstanding territorial controversy.

items.evp_def: The profession, activity, or skill of managing international relations.
items.definition_en: The profession, activity, or skill of managing international relations.
examples: Diplomacy prevailed where military posturing had failed.
Ambassadors must balance firmness with subtle cultural diplomacy.

items.evp_def: Favoring or enforcing strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom.
items.definition_en: Favoring or enforcing strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom.
examples: The report documented the erosion of civil liberties under the authoritarian regime.
Dissidents faced severe censorship in authoritarian states.

items.evp_def: The supreme power or authority of a state to govern itself or another state.
items.definition_en: The supreme power or authority of a state to govern itself or another state.
examples: Treaties must respect the territorial sovereignty of independent member states.
Economic interdependence sometimes complicates traditional concepts of state sovereignty.

items.evp_def: To manipulate the boundaries of an electoral constituency so as to favor one party or class.
items.definition_en: To manipulate the boundaries of an electoral constituency so as to favor one party or class.
items.definition_zh: 不公地改划选区以谋私利
examples: Partisan legislatures attempted to gerrymander congressional districts before the election.
Courts struck down the gerrymandered electoral map for violating voter equity.

items.evp_def: A small group of people having control of a country, organization, or institution.
items.definition_en: A small group of people having control of a country, organization, or institution.
items.definition_zh: 寡头政治，寡头垄断集团
examples: Critics warned that astronomical campaign donations risk turning democracy into an oligarchy.
The transition from monarchy led directly into a commercial oligarchy.

items.evp_def: The quality or state of being in accordance with fact or reality.
items.definition_en: The quality or state of being in accordance with fact or reality.
examples: Philosophers have debated the nature of objective truth for millennia.
Science seeks empirical truth through rigorous observation.

items.evp_def: Reasoning conducted or assessed according to strict principles of validity.
items.definition_en: Reasoning conducted or assessed according to strict principles of validity.
examples: Aristotelian logic laid the groundwork for modern formal syllogisms.
There was an inescapable flaw in the opponent's core logic.

items.evp_def: Moral principles that govern a person's behavior or the conducting of an activity.
items.definition_en: Moral principles that govern a person's behavior or the conducting of an activity.
examples: Bioethics examines ethical dilemmas surrounding genetic engineering.
A philosopher must weigh conflicting duties in virtue ethics.

items.evp_def: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.
items.definition_en: Based on or in accordance with reason or logic.
examples: Descartes championed rational thought as the prime foundation of knowledge.
Emotions should be balanced by rational inquiry.

items.evp_def: Relating to human existence or the existentialist philosophy asserting individual freedom and purpose.
items.definition_en: Relating to human existence or the existentialist philosophy asserting individual freedom and purpose.
items.definition_zh: 存在主义的，关于人类存在的
examples: Sartre addressed the existential burden of absolute personal freedom.
Climate change poses an acute existential crisis for planetary biodiversity.

items.evp_def: The branch of philosophy concerned with knowledge, belief, and the justification of truth claims.
items.definition_en: The branch of philosophy concerned with knowledge, belief, and the justification of truth claims.
examples: Epistemology asks how we can reliably distinguish knowledge from mere opinion.
Kant revolutionized epistemology by proposing synthetic a priori judgments.

items.evp_def: The rejection of all religious and moral principles, often in the belief that life is meaningless.
items.definition_en: The rejection of all religious and moral principles, often in the belief that life is meaningless.
examples: Nietzsche examined the historical emergence of European nihilism.
Existentialism attempted to overcome nihilism by creating subjective purpose.

items.evp_def: The discourse between two opposing viewpoints seeking to establish truth through reasoned arguments.
items.definition_en: The discourse between two opposing viewpoints seeking to establish truth through reasoned arguments.
examples: Hegelian dialectic synthesizes thesis and antithesis into higher comprehension.
Socrates employed rigorous dialectic to expose hidden contradictions.

items.evp_def: The philosophical idea that only one's own mind is sure to exist.
items.definition_en: The philosophical idea that only one's own mind is sure to exist.
examples: Epistemological skepticism taken to its absolute extreme arrives at solipsism.
He dismissed solipsism as an unlivable intellectual novelty.

items.evp_def: A hollow muscular organ that pumps the blood through the circulatory system by rhythmic contraction.
items.definition_en: A hollow muscular organ that pumps the blood through the circulatory system by rhythmic contraction.
examples: Aerobic exercise strengthens your heart muscles.
His heart beat rapidly during the thrilling presentation.

items.evp_def: The internal organ in which the first major part of digestion of food occurs.
items.definition_en: The internal organ in which the first major part of digestion of food occurs.
examples: You shouldn't consume spicy food on an empty stomach.
Gastric juices inside the stomach break down dietary proteins.

items.evp_def: An organ of soft nervous tissue contained in the skull, coordinating sensation and intellectual activity.
items.definition_en: An organ of soft nervous tissue contained in the skull, coordinating sensation and intellectual activity.
examples: The human brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons.
Adequate sleep allows the brain to flush metabolic waste.

items.evp_def: Each of the pair of organs situated within the rib cage, allowing oxygen exchange with blood.
items.definition_en: Each of the pair of organs situated within the rib cage, allowing oxygen exchange with blood.
examples: Inhaling fresh alpine air expanded his lungs.
Smoking damages delicate alveoli within human lung tissue.

items.evp_def: A large lobed glandular organ in the abdomen, involved in metabolism, bile secretion, and detoxification.
items.definition_en: A large lobed glandular organ in the abdomen, involved in metabolism, bile secretion, and detoxification.
examples: The liver possesses a remarkable capacity to regenerate cellular tissue.
Excessive alcohol consumption places severe strain on liver function.

items.evp_def: Each of a pair of organs in the abdominal cavity that excrete urine and regulate electrolyte balance.
items.definition_en: Each of a pair of organs in the abdominal cavity that excrete urine and regulate electrolyte balance.
examples: The kidneys continuously filter metabolic toxins from circulating bloodstream.
Drinking ample water prevents kidney stone formation.

items.evp_def: Any of the muscular-walled tubes forming part of the circulation system conveying oxygenated blood from the heart.
items.definition_en: Any of the muscular-walled tubes forming part of the circulation system conveying oxygenated blood from the heart.
examples: Coronary arteries deliver vital oxygenated blood directly to cardiac muscle.
Arterial elasticity typically declines with advancing age.

items.evp_def: A large gland behind the stomach that secretes digestive enzymes and the hormone insulin.
items.definition_en: A large gland behind the stomach that secretes digestive enzymes and the hormone insulin.
examples: Beta cells within the pancreas synthesize and release insulin.
Inflammation of the pancreas requires immediate clinical intervention.

items.evp_def: A layer at the back of the eyeball sensitive to light, triggering nerve impulses via optic nerves.
items.definition_en: A layer at the back of the eyeball sensitive to light, triggering nerve impulses via optic nerves.
examples: Photoreceptor rods and cones in the retina convert light into electrical impulses.
Laser surgery can effectively repair a torn retina.

items.evp_def: The part of the brain at the back of the skull coordinating muscular activity and balance.
items.definition_en: The part of the brain at the back of the skull coordinating muscular activity and balance.
examples: The cerebellum fine-tunes motor execution and maintains dynamic equilibrium.
Damage to the cerebellum leads to ataxia and compromised motor coordination.

items.evp_def: The muscular tube connecting the throat with the stomach.
items.definition_en: The muscular tube connecting the throat with the stomach.
examples: Peristaltic muscle contractions propel ingested food through the esophagus.
Gastroesophageal reflux causes irritating acid into the lower esophagus.

items.evp_def: Feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.
items.definition_en: Feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.
examples: The children were happy playing in the sunlit meadow.
We celebrated a happy family reunion.

items.evp_def: Feeling or showing strong annoyance, displeasure, or hostility.
items.definition_en: Feeling or showing strong annoyance, displeasure, or hostility.
examples: He grew angry when he discovered the broken promise.
Take ten deep breaths before responding to an angry message.

items.evp_def: Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.
items.definition_en: Feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements and advantages.
examples: Try not to be jealous of other people's overnight success.
Jealousy often stems from deep-seated personal insecurity.

items.evp_def: Characterized by or exhibiting a sentimental yearning for the happiness felt in a former place, time, or situation.
items.definition_en: Characterized by or exhibiting a sentimental yearning for the happiness felt in a former place, time, or situation.
examples: Hearing the vintage jazz tune made him feel deeply nostalgic.
Flipping through grandmother's photo albums evokes nostalgic warmth.

items.evp_def: The complete loss or absence of hope.
items.definition_en: The complete loss or absence of hope.
items.definition_zh: 绝望，令人绝望的人或事
examples: She refused to yield to despair despite severe setbacks.
Kind words from a mentor rescued the student from despair.

items.evp_def: The state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled.
items.definition_en: The state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled.
examples: Watching mountain peaks shrouded in morning mist brought immense serenity.
Her innate serenity steadied the entire emergency team.

items.evp_def: Bitter indignation at having been treated unfairly.
items.definition_en: Bitter indignation at having been treated unfairly.
examples: Harboring unspoken resentment corrodes interpersonal intimacy.
Unfair salary disparities bred intense resentment across the division.

items.evp_def: A state of intense excitement and happiness.
items.definition_en: A state of intense excitement and happiness.
examples: Marathon runners often experience runner's high accompanied by profound euphoria.
The euphoria of championship victory lasted for weeks.

items.evp_def: A feeling of pensive sadness, typically with no obvious cause.
items.definition_en: A feeling of pensive sadness, typically with no obvious cause.
examples: Chopin's nocturnes convey a haunting lyrical melancholy.
An autumn drizzle infused the quiet streets with gentle melancholy.

items.evp_def: A feeling of intense irritation or annoyance.
items.definition_en: A feeling of intense irritation or annoyance.
examples: He threw up his hands in sheer exasperation at the bureaucratic runaround.
Repeated technical malfunctions provoked widespread exasperation among attendees.

items.evp_def: A long curved fruit which grows in clusters and has soft pulpy flesh and yellow skin when ripe.
items.definition_en: A long curved fruit which grows in clusters and has soft pulpy flesh and yellow skin when ripe.
examples: Ripe bananas provide an instant boost of potassium and natural energy.
Peel the banana before blending it into the morning smoothie.

items.evp_def: A round juicy citrus fruit with a tough bright reddish-yellow rind.
items.definition_en: A round juicy citrus fruit with a tough bright reddish-yellow rind.
examples: Squeeze fresh oranges for a glass of vitamin C rich breakfast juice.
Valencia oranges are celebrated for their juicy sweetness.

items.evp_def: A sweet soft red fruit with a seed-studded surface.
items.definition_en: A sweet soft red fruit with a seed-studded surface.
examples: Fresh strawberries and whipped cream form an iconic Wimbledon dessert.
We picked wild strawberries along the meadow border.

items.evp_def: The large fruit of a plant of the gourd family, with smooth green skin and sweet watery red pulp.
items.definition_en: The large fruit of a plant of the gourd family, with smooth green skin and sweet watery red pulp.
examples: Chilled watermelon slices are quintessential treats on sultry summer afternoons.
Seedless watermelons have become widespread in grocery markets.

items.evp_def: A round stone fruit with juicy yellow flesh and downy pinkish-yellow skin.
items.definition_en: A round stone fruit with juicy yellow flesh and downy pinkish-yellow skin.
examples: Ripe peaches smell heavenly when harvested in midsummer.
Grandmother baked a southern-style warm peach cobbler.

items.evp_def: The small sweet blue-black edible berry of an extensive genus of shrubs.
items.definition_en: The small sweet blue-black edible berry of an extensive genus of shrubs.
examples: Blueberries are packed with potent antioxidants and dietary fiber.
Add a handful of fresh blueberries to the pancake batter.

items.evp_def: A spherical fruit with a tough reddish rind containing jewel-like ruby seeds enclosed in juicy pulp.
items.definition_en: A spherical fruit with a tough reddish rind containing jewel-like ruby seeds enclosed in juicy pulp.
examples: Sprinkle tart pomegranate seeds across the roasted walnut salad.
Pomegranate juice is revered in Persian cuisine for its depth.

items.evp_def: An edible fruit that resembles a large tomato and has sweet orange flesh when soft and ripe.
items.definition_en: An edible fruit that resembles a large tomato and has sweet orange flesh when soft and ripe.
examples: Unripe persimmons are intensely astringent due to high soluble tannin levels.
Hachiya persimmons must soften to jelly-like consistency before eating.

items.evp_def: A tropical fruit with thick dark purple rind and fragrant, sweet, segmented white flesh, hailed as the queen of fruits.
items.definition_en: A tropical fruit with thick dark purple rind and fragrant, sweet, segmented white flesh, hailed as the queen of fruits.
examples: The delicate snow-white segments of mangosteen offer a luscious floral sweetness.
Southeast Asian street stalls display pyramids of freshly harvested mangosteen.

items.evp_def: A starchy plant tuber that is one of the most important food crops worldwide.
items.definition_en: A starchy plant tuber that is one of the most important food crops worldwide.
examples: Mashed potatoes seasoned with butter and chives accompany the steak.
Boil the potatoes until tender to make potato salad.

items.evp_def: A glossy red, or occasionally yellow, pulpy edible fruit eaten as a vegetable or in salad.
items.definition_en: A glossy red, or occasionally yellow, pulpy edible fruit eaten as a vegetable or in salad.
examples: Sun-ripened tomatoes possess sweet acidity ideal for pasta sauce.
Slice heirloom tomatoes with fresh mozzarella and basil.

items.evp_def: A tapering orange-colored root eaten as a vegetable.
items.definition_en: A tapering orange-colored root eaten as a vegetable.
examples: Carrots contain high concentrations of beta-carotene beneficial for eye health.
Grate raw carrots finely for an aromatic spiced cake.

items.evp_def: A swollen edible bulb with a pungent taste and smell, composed of several concentric layers.
items.definition_en: A swollen edible bulb with a pungent taste and smell, composed of several concentric layers.
examples: Sauté diced onions slowly in olive oil until golden and caramelized.
Chopping raw onions releases sulfurous vapors that cause tearing.

items.evp_def: A cultivated variety of cabbage bearing heads of green or purplish flower buds.
items.definition_en: A cultivated variety of cabbage bearing heads of green or purplish flower buds.
examples: Steamed broccoli preserves vital micronutrients and retains a vibrant green hue.
Toss roasted broccoli with minced garlic and grated parmesan.

items.evp_def: An edible flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae with dark green succulent leaves.
items.definition_en: An edible flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae with dark green succulent leaves.
examples: Fresh baby spinach wilts within seconds when tossed into hot soup.
Spinach is renowned for iron and folate content.

items.evp_def: A tall plant of the lily family with fine feathery foliage, cultivated for its tender edible young shoots.
items.definition_en: A tall plant of the lily family with fine feathery foliage, cultivated for its tender edible young shoots.
examples: Grill tender green asparagus spears with a drizzle of lemon oil.
Snap off the woody bottom ends of asparagus before cooking.

items.evp_def: A small variety of vegetable marrow; a summer squash with green skin.
items.definition_en: A small variety of vegetable marrow; a summer squash with green skin.
examples: Spiralized zucchini ribbons make a nutritious low-carb pasta alternative.
Bake grated zucchini into moist cinnamon loaves.

items.evp_def: A European plant cultivated for its large thistle-like flower heads, the fleshy bases of which are edible.
items.definition_en: A European plant cultivated for its large thistle-like flower heads, the fleshy bases of which are edible.
examples: Steam whole globe artichokes and dip the fleshy bract leaves in garlic butter.
Marinated artichoke hearts are standard fixtures in Mediterranean antipasti.

items.evp_def: A cultivated cabbage of a variety with an edible swollen stem resembling a turnip.
items.definition_en: A cultivated cabbage of a variety with an edible swollen stem resembling a turnip.
examples: Raw kohlrabi delivers a crisp, mildly sweet crunch reminiscent of water chestnuts.
Julienne crisp kohlrabi into an apple slaw.

items.evp_def: A domestic fowl kept for its eggs or meat, especially the flesh eaten as food.
items.definition_en: A domestic fowl kept for its eggs or meat, especially the flesh eaten as food.
examples: Roast chicken seasoned with rosemary makes a classic Sunday dinner.
Skinless chicken breasts provide lean protein for athletes.

items.evp_def: The flesh of a cow, bull, or ox, used as food.
items.definition_en: The flesh of a cow, bull, or ox, used as food.
examples: Slow-simmered beef stew fills the kitchen with savory warmth.
Wagyu beef is renowned worldwide for exquisite marbling.

items.evp_def: The flesh of a pig used as food, especially when uncured.
items.definition_en: The flesh of a pig used as food, especially when uncured.
examples: Braised pork belly is a cornerstone of Chinese home-style gastronomy.
Glaze tender pork tenderloin with apple cider and mustard.

items.evp_def: A large edible fish with pink flesh, celebrated for rich omega-3 fatty acids.
items.definition_en: A large edible fish with pink flesh, celebrated for rich omega-3 fatty acids.
examples: Pan-sear wild Atlantic salmon skin-side down until wonderfully crispy.
Smoked salmon and cream cheese are beloved bagel toppings.

items.evp_def: A small free-swimming crustacean with an elongated body, highly prized as seafood.
